boundTo.note: Not yet bound to a record. Record 0036 requires these proofs to be green before F-6 and F-11 may be carried into the closing evidence, and before the long gates run.

why: Record 0033 declared F-6 and F-11 closed on the strength of the change alone. Record 0036 rejected that: a correction without a test that fails on the uncorrected code is an assertion, not a proof. Each invariant below is therefore paired with a mutation that removes exactly it, and the run that shows the specs go red.

proofs.subject: src/ViciOne.ServiceBus/JobService/JobService/JobService.cs
proofs.howItIsObservedWithoutWideningTheApi: Every lifecycle transition announces itself by publishing a SetConcurrentJobLimit that names its own ConcurrentLimitKind. A publish endpoint double therefore tells a stop, a start and a heartbeat apart, can hold one of them open, and can fail one -- with no member added to the job service. Job acceptance is observed through the real StartJob path over a consume context from the in-memory bus, not a hand-built double: the rejection path constructs a ConsumeJobContext and notifies a fault through the receive context, and a double would have had to reproduce the very thing under proof.

mutations.expected: a start can overtake a running stop
a stop can overtake a running start

mutations.removes: setting the stopping state before the drain
mutations.expected: jobs are still accepted while the stop drains

mutations.removes: disposing the previous heartbeat when a start begins
mutations.expected: each start hangs another timer beside the running one

mutations.removes: closing job acceptance again when a start fails
mutations.expected: a running service whose restart fails keeps taking jobs although its heartbeat is already gone
mutations.note: Survived the first round of specs and is the reason there are ten and not nine. The first four specs all failed out of an already stopped service, where the stopping state is set either way -- so the mutation was invisible. Only a service that was running when the restart failed distinguishes them.

proofs.notClaimed: The StopHeartbeat() in the failure path of BusStarted is not reachable on the current ordering: the timer is created last, and the only statement after it cannot throw. It is kept as a guard against a future reordering and is stated here as untested rather than counted as proven.

mutations.removes: the rethrow, restoring the delivered defect
mutations.expected: the harness starts against a virtual host that could not be prepared

mutations.removes: the bare rethrow in favour of "throw ex"
mutations.expected: the stack of the original throw site is discarded
mutations.note: Survived the first version of the spec, which asserted that the trace named the calling fixture. That assertion was worthless: an exception leaving an async method is captured and rethrown at the await, which appends the caller's frames whether the stack was preserved or reconstructed. The spec now asserts a named frame from below the catch, which only a preserved stack can carry.

mutations.removes: the trimming of the close reason, so closing throws on a long failure message
mutations.expected: nothing -- a failing close must not change what the caller receives

mutations.removes: additionally the best effort handling of the close failure
mutations.expected: the close failure replaces the real cause at the caller
mutations.note: This pair is what makes the previous row evidence rather than an inert mutation: because rethrowing the close failure does change the outcome, the close demonstrably ran and demonstrably failed in the row above -- and the caller still received the setup failure.

mutationTooling.note: The mutations are applied to a working copy and reverted from a byte identical backup after every run. No mutation is part of the delivered tree; the working tree was verified clean against the backup after the last run.
